S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

symptom.disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder defined by persistent disturbances such as hallucinations, delusions, disorganized speech or behavior, and negative symptoms, with functional decline and a course lasting at least six months. It is distinguished from brief psychotic disorders by duration, from mood disorders with psychosis by the absence of a primary mood episode driving the psychosis, and from substance- or medical-induced psychosis by the lack of a better explanatory cause.

patient.stressor_event: Major change in responsibilities at work (e.g., promotion, demotion)
patient.stressor: When Alicia’s Austin company entered a major expansion and she took on direct responsibility for a new arts-and-commerce division, the looser creative schedule that had once suited her became a liability under constant board scrutiny. Over the next 2 years and 4 months, colleagues first noticed that she was missing strategic follow-through, then that her responses in meetings and at gallery-related events became increasingly inappropriate to the setting, while her former warmth, curiosity, and initiative steadily receded. Her work performance deteriorated enough that her husband began informally handling household obligations and senior staff quietly redistributed executive decisions she could no longer manage. She came to psychiatric care after a board retreat ended abruptly because her behavior disrupted the proceedings and her husband accompanied her to an urgent psychiatric evaluation.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: I came in because I keep hearing people talking about me through the conference room walls or from my phone even when it’s off, usually board members or staff saying I’m ruining the company, and it sounds so clear that I answer them before I realize no one else heard it.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: In meetings or gallery events I’ll suddenly stand up, rearrange pens or name cards into patterns, repeat a phrase someone just said, or hold my hands in the air like I’m presenting something, even though I know afterward it made no sense for the room.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: I used to be the person driving every idea and calling people after openings, but now I can sit at my desk for hours staring at the agenda, barely speak to my husband or staff, and feel almost nothing about work I used to love.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’m no longer reliably able to run the division or keep up with basic executive decisions, and senior staff have quietly taken over work I used to handle myself. At home, my husband has had to manage most household responsibilities because I leave things unfinished or do not start them at all.
add_requirements.duration: This has been building for about 2 years and 4 months, since the company expansion put me in charge of the new arts-and-commerce division.
add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_duration: The voices from the walls or my phone have been happening for about the past 3 months.
